summary: Extend the reference to cover the quoted passage: 75/165–167
rationale: The example begins with “šləḥle gawe d-u=ṣafuro” in 75/165, continues with “mnaḏ̣afle w-maḥatle ʕal qarʕe d-ruḥe” in 75/166, and ends with “daqana d-lo=məḥze u=šufr-ayḏe” in 75/167. All three consecutive verses are needed. The automatic alternative 75/166 alone also covers only part of the quotation.

summary: Mark the existing JL 7.7.11 quotation as cut.
rationale: The source continues with har lo=mədwoṣiwa; retain inherited spelling and signal the omitted finite predicate rather than presenting a complete sentence.

summary: Mark the matching German cut.

summary: JL 17.6.6 g-ḥozí-way-na-le belongs to Infectum-wa.
rationale: ḥoz- is the Infectum base and -way-na- the 1pl -wa formation; not a Preterit agent-suffix form.

summary: The cave-discovery example belongs to finding, sense 2.
rationale: Explicit discovery of the cave first; independently matched in PrS 41/35. Keep inherited page/verse reference until concordance is checked.

summary: JL 7.7.11 is a parenthetical conversational appeal.
rationale: Second-person ko-ḥozət intervenes in the account; repeated parallel forms support new construction 1b.

summary: 73/316 is deliberative ascertainment, not ensuring performance.
rationale: The question aydarbo k-saymina asks how to act; it does not state monitoring or causing an action.

summary: 75/167 d-lo=məḥze is Detransitive Infectum.
rationale: məḥze is the prefixed Detransitive Infectum form in a purpose clause, unlike finite Detransitive ḥze/ḥazi.

summary: Cognate u=ḥzoyo in MM 80 belongs to active Infinitiv.
rationale: The same observer sees; the noun reinforces ḥzeli and asserts no Detransitive predication.

summary: Move the ḥozi-way-na-le example to Infectum-wa
rationale: The verb illustrating ḥzy is “g-ḥozí-way-na-le”, an Infectum ḥozi- form with -wa, not a Preterit form. Its form agrees with the existing Infectum-wa example “lə=ḥozí-way-na-le” at 63/308. The supplied JL 17.6/6 text confirms gḥoziwaynale. Retain sense 2.

summary: File the passive məḥze example under Detransitive Infectum
rationale: The form illustrating ḥzy is “məḥze” in the purpose clause “daqana d-lo=məḥze u=šufr-ayḏe”. This is Detransitive Infectum, with m-, rather than the Detransitive Preterit ḥze illustrated by the Gabriel example in this same box. The preceding preterites belong to other roots. Create the Detransitive Infectum box if absent and retain detransitive sense 1.

summary: New box Infinitiv: example for sense 1 in Infinitiv (MAC Ishaq Material culture/42)

data.turoyo: Yani, ono, u+medano lo+ʕayəšne bas ḥzalli ḥzoyo, bas ḥzoyo.
data.translation: Like, I, this thing, I didn’t experience it (lit. ‘live it’), but I saw things, just things (lit. ‘I saw them seeing, just seeing’).

rationale: Active Infinitiv cognate complement; observation contrasted with lived participation. Repeated noun shares one quotation.

summary: New box Infectum: example for sense 1 in Infectum (PrS 16/41)

data.turoyo: I səsto d Rustam mi hawa yo, lo kməḥzoyo.
data.translation: Wie gesagt, war das Pferd Rustem's von Luft und daher nicht sichtbar.

rationale: First Detransitive Infectum box: nonvisibility with feminine subject.

summary: New box Infinitiv: example for sense 2 in Infinitiv (PrS 64/114)

data.turoyo: Aḥna ḥzoyo ḥəzyolan.
data.translation: Wir haben sie gefunden.

rationale: New active Infinitiv sense-2 cell; edition omits the cognate reinforcement but preserves the complete assertion.

summary: New box Infinitiv: example for sense 1 in Infinitiv (102/69)

data.turoyo: “Pak lu šuġlo rabano! U kurrəkano dlo ḥzoyo lo ṭləbleli, yawma eli w ele ḥzelan ḥḏoḏe w maʕǧablan ḥḏoḏe w adlalyo keləm lo kobe aʕmi, lo kobe w lo kšoqəl aʕmi, haṯi mən masale yo?”
data.translation: Was ist denn das für eine seltsame Sache! Der Junge hat nicht um mich gefreit, ohne mich gesehen zu haben. Heute haben wir einander gesehen, und wir haben gefallen an einander gefunden, und heute Nacht spricht er kein Wart mit mir und hat keinen Umgang mit mir. Was ist das für eine Sache? -

rationale: Active Infinitiv in a without-seeing clause; retained nominal separation from batch 1. Full paired seeing context disambiguates the participants.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 1.12/450)

data.turoyo: Kətwola diwanxana, mi diwanxana məḥzəyowa i qalʕo d Mərde.
data.translation: It had a reception hall; from the reception hall the citadel of Mardin could be seen.

rationale: First Detransitive Infectum-wa cell after round 1; explicit feminine theme, source/viewpoint and absent observer.

summary: New box Infectum: example for sense 1 in Infectum (Jan 2.12/2840)

data.turoyo: I naqqa d məḥze u ʕamal, kmiḏoʕo i həmme du ʕaməl.
data.translation: When the work is seen, the resolve of the worker becomes known.

rationale: Thin Detransitive Infectum 1 cell; nonpersonal theme and generic relation to knowing.

summary: New box Infectum: example for sense 1 in Infectum (Jan 2.31/4855)

data.turoyo: U rozo ǧawhar yo, u ǧawharano diḏe, yaʕni maǧhul yo, lə kməḥze.
data.translation: The mystery is an essence, and that essence of it, I mean, is unknown; it is not seen.

rationale: Thin Detransitive Infectum 1 cell; abstract invisible theme in theological discourse.

summary: New sense 1b: parenthetisch: „siehst du, weißt du“, Hinweis auf geteiltes Wissen oder eine Erklärung

data.label: 1b
data.gloss: parenthetisch: „siehst du, weißt du“, Hinweis auf geteiltes Wissen oder eine Erklärung

rationale: Repeated objectless second-person forms interrupt accounts and address the listener; this is a recurrent conversational construction, not a separate physical seeing event.

summary: New sense 2b: (jdn./etw.) für ... halten, als ... ansehen (auch mit b-ṣife d-)

data.label: 2b
data.gloss: (jdn./etw.) für ... halten, als ... ansehen (auch mit b-ṣife d-)

rationale: An experiencer evaluates an object with a secondary predicate; distinct from the dative-experiencer seeming frame in sense 5. Existing sense 2 already has a munasəb example.

summary: New sense 1b: als Hinweis oder Aufforderung zur Aufmerksamkeit: „siehst du, weißt du; sieh, gib acht“

data.label: 1b
data.gloss: als Hinweis oder Aufforderung zur Aufmerksamkeit: „siehst du, weißt du; sieh, gib acht“

rationale: Repeated objectless second-person forms interrupt accounts and address the listener; this is a recurrent conversational construction, not a separate physical seeing event. Batch 2 supplies recurring objectless Imperativ attention calls; include these in the same construction.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (Bilgic Hochzeit und Tod/20)

data.turoyo: Zəxyo bəṯr u bayto, ḥzay, mə kito.
data.translation: geh hinter das Haus, und schau, was es dort gibt

rationale: Imperativ sense 1 has three examples; a short independent instruction with an embedded question.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (Hors 2/22)

data.turoyo: W zux, ḥzaya
data.translation: Geh hin, sieh sie dir an!

rationale: Second addition to the thin Imperativ sense-1 cell; retains the feminine object suffix verbatim.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Hors 2/136)

data.turoyo: Əmmo: "Ya babo, ono kəḏʕono, ono u mede, d ḥəzyowaynole mu ʕarbawo, d kətwa aʕmi, hiye ste xtoṯi wa, kəmmono, hama w lo kəḏʕono."
data.translation: ,, Vater, nach allem, was ich von dem Gazellenbock zu sehen gewohnt war, der bei mir war, möchte ich sagen, auch er war wie ich.Und ich weiß nicht ..."

rationale: Distinct feminine Infectum-wa shape with habitual experiential context; morphology remains explicitly provisional.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (JL 12.14/3)

data.turoyo: W me d maḥtiwayna ṣawʕan ebe ḥoziwayna, aṯi l taqṭoro l=aṯi.
data.translation: Wenn wir unseren Finger hineinsteckten, sahen wir, ob sie soweit (abgekühlt) war, daß man sie stocken lassen konnte, oder noch nicht.

rationale: Unusual tactile test plus alternative-question complement improves the context beyond the four existing visual Infectum-wa examples.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit-wa (JTM 3.2/3)

data.turoyo: I ḥkume darke stene, ḥzanwunne lak kurmanǧ, aṯən ʕam ḥḏoḏe w hǧəmme ʕal aṣ ṣuroye.
data.translation: Die „hiesige Regierung“ hatte sich die Kurden ausgesucht. Sie vereinigten sich und fielen über die Christen her.

rationale: Preterit-wa finding has no securely filed example after the corrections; l-marked human object and contracted suffix chain.

summary: example for sense 2b in Infectum (JTM 5.1/23)

data.turoyo: kḥuzalla b ṣife d gawro
data.translation: sie sehen sie als Mann an

rationale: First example of the new evaluative construction 2b with b ṣife d gawro.

summary: example for sense 2b in Infectum (JTM 5.2/89)

data.turoyo: qay luno kḥuzatli naʕimo?
data.translation: Hältst du mich etwa für zu jung?

rationale: New 2b construction: overt first-person object and adjective, contrasted in the verse with ḥšw.

summary: example for sense 2b in Preterit (24/221)

data.turoyo: Bal hawxa ḥzelan munasəb.
data.translation: Aber so haben wir es passend gefunden.

rationale: New Preterit cell for evaluative construction 2b; clear propositional evaluation.

summary: example for sense 4 in Imperativ (JTM 5.3/60)

data.turoyo: ḥzay mə kumannux, d lo qquṭaʕno qarʕux uʕdo ha.
data.translation: Tu, was ich dir sage, sonst schlage ich dir jetzt den Kopf ab!

rationale: Sparse Imperativ sense 4: an instruction to heed and comply with speech content.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit-wa (Lahdo Traitor 2/54)

data.turoyo: ono naʕimo i emo d babi ḥzewayla u sayfo.
data.translation: when I was still little, the mother of my father had experienced the genocide.

rationale: Preterit-wa sense 1 has two examples; overt feminine experiencer and historical experience.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (MAC Besim History of Bsorino/11)

data.turoyo: Mšayele, ḥəḷḷe, naʕime latte, ʕəmrayye dmaṭi, dəmmina, bəṯr maḥ+ḥamši, ŭ gəzzewa, azólowa lu+Qudəs.
data.translation: He inquired, he saw, they didn’t have children, that their age had reached (lit. ‘their age, that it had reached’), let’s say, over fifty, and he would go, he was going to Jerusalem.

rationale: Unusual contracted lateral form ḥəḷḷe, independently comparable with ḥəlle at /21.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit (MAC Besim History of Bsorino/22)

data.turoyo: Ḥzélele šaqfo tamo, ʕbədle tamo, si+qriṯo d Aspəs.
data.translation: He found himself a crag there, he served (God) there, by the village of Aspəs.

rationale: Distinct agent plus coreferential beneficiary suffix sequence in ḥzélele.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit-wa (MAC Besim History of Bsorino/35)

data.turoyo: Ḥa manne ḥzélewa bu+ḥəlmo, məḷḷe, ‘Gdoṯelan hadiye rabṯo’.
data.translation: One of them had seen in a dream, he said, ‘A great gift will come to us’.

rationale: Sparse Preterit-wa sense 1; -wa follows the agent suffix, contrasting with inherited pre-agent -wo-.

summary: example for sense 2 in Imperativ (MAC Murder in Kfarze, The Testimony of Farida/19)

data.turoyo: ánnaqqa zoxu, ayko dkəbʕutu, ḥzāwle, qṭálŭle.

rationale: Imperativ sense 2 has two examples; clear indexed masculine patient.

evidence.cite: MAC Murder in Kfarze, The Testimony of Farida/19

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (MAC NE Habirman Xatun/21)

data.turoyo: Kalko ḥzélәlxu harke. Toxu!
data.translation: I’ve just seen you here. Come back!

rationale: Distinct compact first-person agent plus second-person plural object suffixes; preserved without paradigm normalization.

summary: example for sense 1b in Preterit (MAC NE Interview 2/54)

data.turoyo: ǧġeni mu+dyoqo, dínaqqa dəmmiwa, ḥzelax, dəmmiwa ḥe haye...
data.translation: Besides crushing, when they would say, you know, they would sing ḥe haye...

rationale: New subsense 1b in Preterit; clear feminine addressee and parenthetical position.

summary: example for sense 1b in Preterit (MAC NE Interview 2/151)

data.turoyo: Ḥzelux talisat latwa, ŭ naylonat mani lə+nfəqle.
data.translation: You see (lit. ‘you saw’), there were no sacks, and these nylon bags hadn’t come out.

rationale: New 1b with an explanatory proposition and explicit edition note on Preterit form.

summary: example for sense 2 in Imperativ (PrS 23/2)

data.turoyo: Zox, krax b briṯo, kraxlan ʕal tloṯ aḥwoṯo, ḥzilanne, gəzzan ṭəlbinalle.

rationale: Thin Imperativ sense 2 plus beneficiary/object suffix sequence; edition conditional retained, parse questioned.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (PrS 38/90)

data.turoyo: Ḥzanxu?
data.translation: Habt ihr nun gesehen?

rationale: Unusual second-person plural Preterit form; not treated as a new meaning solely from German.

summary: example for sense 1 in ko-Preterit (PrS 72/18)

data.turoyo: ʕAbər u malaxo l riše, kḥəzele l more dak kallat, šqile ruḥe dawo, d kətne kallat aʕle, w daʕiri tavda more dak kallat w u malaxo.
data.translation: da sah er den Todesengel zu jenem hereintreten, und der Engel nahm die Seele des Schuldners; darauf kehrten sie miteinander zurück, der Reiche und der Engel.

rationale: Thin ko-Preterit sense 1: k- attaches to the Preterit base; participant direction is flagged for checking.

summary: example for sense 3 in Infectum (3/51)

data.turoyo: Aṭ ṭarfone b riše daṣ ṣawʕoṯo ne. Bann iḏoṯo kḥuzena šuġlone ġalabe.
data.translation: Die Nägel befinden sich am Ende der Finger. Mit den Händen verrichten wir viele arbeiten.

rationale: First Infectum example for already established sense 3, with hands as instrument.

summary: example for sense 3 in Infectum (3/54)

data.turoyo: Aṣ ṣawʕoṯo kḥozən šuġlone, xəd u ḥayṭo w xəd u dyoqo d ṭambur.
data.translation: Die Finger verrichten Tätigkeiten wie das Nähen und das Lautenschlagen.

rationale: Second sense-3 example contrasts fingers as metonymic actors with the preceding human actor.

summary: example for sense 2 in ko-Preterit (6/76)

data.turoyo: U lalyawo kḥəzalle, kmarḥəbi b ḥḏoḏe ġalabe.
data.translation: Am Abend finden sie ihn, und sie begrüßen einander herzlich.

rationale: First example for ko-Preterit sense 2; preserves the Preterit base with k-.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infinitiv (24/258)

data.turoyo: me d maṭən lu ʕumro daḥ ḥamšaḥṣar əšne, štaḥṣar, bayo d kətwayye bi ḥzayto ġalabe layəq šafire
data.translation: Als sie nun ins fünfzehnte, sechzehnte Lebens Jahr traten, waren sie sehr hübsch und schön anzusehen

rationale: Sparse Detransitive Infinitiv appearance cell: bi ḥzayto specifies appearance; nominal status explicitly qualified.

summary: example for sense 3 in Infectum (28/55)

data.turoyo: Adyawma hani ḥamməš əšne, haqqayəṣ kḥozət, xadame qumi, yawmo lo məllux masala "mən hat? mən mede? m ayko hat? w šəkəl diḏux mən yo?"
data.translation: Heute sind es fünf Jahre, daß du dienst vor mir verrichtest. Du hast niemals zu mir etwa gesagt: Was bist du eigentlich? Was bist du für ein Ding? Woher bist du? Was bist du denn eigentlich?"

rationale: Already established sense 3, Infectum: service object xadame contrasts with earlier šuġlone; cumulative cell remains below five.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (35/23)

data.turoyo: W ono koḥozeno, d u ḥeloqo du papazano bam maye dlo sabab ġalaṭ w ḥṭiṯo.
data.translation: Ich finde aber, diesen geistlichen ohne Grund ins Wasser zu werfen, ist ein Fehler und eine Sünde.

rationale: Clear independent ethical judgment with d-clause supplies a substantially different context from concrete perception; retained under broad sense 1.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (40/17)

data.turoyo: Qay yo ḥzelux bi xədmayḏe, xdəmle bi ʕito. Hawo mḥasadle mene."
data.translation: Warum? Du hast ja gesehen, wie er in der Kirche ministriert hat; dieser hat ihn beneidet."

rationale: Distinct b-marked service expression with bare Preterit, contrasting with concrete and clausal visual stimuli.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infinitiv (42/6)

data.turoyo: Hano, u ṭaboxo, komalle: "Aḥunux u sobo kəmšayəl b kef diḏux w hawi lḥiqoyo l ḥzaytayḏux."
data.translation: Der Koch sprach zu ihm: "Dein Bruder, der alte, läßt dich grüßen, und er sehnt sich danach, dich zu sehen."

rationale: Sparse appearance/seeing nominal cell: possessor is the person seen, not the observer; l- is governed by longing.

summary: example for sense 1b in Imperativ (43/24)

data.turoyo: Aḥuno, ḥzi! Mə kəbʕat, gdobinalux w zux b darbux!
data.translation: Hör freund! Wir werden dir geben, was du willst, aber dann geh deiner Wege!

rationale: First Imperativ example of construction 1b; edition Hör retained as an attention-call rendering.

summary: example for sense 4 in Imperativ (45/20)

data.turoyo: Ba hat ḥzi, ayko koḥozatla, munasəb, səmla dukṯo!
data.translation: Sieh du doch zu! Mach ihr einen Platz da, wo du es geeignet für sie findest!

rationale: Sparse Imperativ sense 4: assignment of responsibility for providing a place, with complete practical instruction.

summary: example for sense 2b in Infectum (58/182)

data.turoyo: Kḥozenanne, hawxa šafire!
data.translation: Ich finde sie so schön!

rationale: New construction 2b: plural objects plus quality predicate; explicit evaluation.

summary: example for sense 3 in Preterit (73/26)

data.turoyo: Zʕure d šulṭone ne, lo nafiqi larwal, lo ḥzalle lo karwuṯo, lo ḥzalle šuġlo, lo ḥzalle mede.
data.translation: Es sind ja Sultanssöhne, sind nie herausgekommen, haben nie Karawanenhandel getrieben, keine Arbeit getan und nichts erlebt.

rationale: First Preterit example for sense 3; the full short contrast keeps work apart from general experience.

summary: example for sense 2b in Infectum (77/136)

data.turoyo: Ono masalan kḥozeno i ḥewarto šafərto. Hat gdəmmət: "Lo! I kamto šafərto yo!"
data.translation: Oder ich finde zum Beispiel die weiße schön, und du sagst: Nein! Die schwarze ist schön.

rationale: Fills construction 2b with an explicit feminine nominal object and adjective; no dative-experiencer analysis.

summary: example for sense 2 in ko-Preterit (81/5)

data.turoyo: Aṯi, məlle li aṯto omər: "Ya ḥurma!" Omər: "Adyawma kal koḥzeli mede ġalabe ṭowo."
data.translation: Zu Hause angekommen, sprach er zu seiner Frau: "Frau, heute habe ich etwas sehr Schönes gefunden."

rationale: Sparse cumulative ko-Preterit sense 2: first-person discovery relevant now.

summary: example for sense 2 in ko-Preterit (81/50)

data.turoyo: Ašər u malkayḏi disa koḥzeli qaduro ḥreno d dahwo.
data.translation: Mein König, ich habe noch einen Topf mit Gold gefunden.

rationale: Sparse ko-Preterit finding cell; explicit found object.

summary: example for sense 2b in Infectum (89/14)

data.turoyo: W hat xort mlayəq hat, koḥozena mlayəq diḏux.
data.translation: Und du bist ein hübscher Bursch, und ich finde, daß sie zu dir paßt.

rationale: Construction 2b now has five cumulative Infectum examples, including suitability with an indexed feminine object.

summary: example for sense 2 in ko-Preterit (91/38)

data.turoyo: Ašər koḥzeli mʕarṯo harke, itoxu!
data.translation: Hallo, ich habe hier eine Höhle gefunden, kommt!

rationale: Sparse cumulative ko-Preterit sense 2; complete discovery announcement.

summary: example for sense 3 in Infectum (94/385)

data.turoyo: I čamkayo, d kətyo b iḏe du mḥalqono, yaʕni du məštaʕyono, ham komḥaləq u pallo w kəmčalqazle w ham ste komakili i maṣafa, d bayn lu pallo w li ḥəlle eba, yaʕni koḥəzyo a tlaṯ waḏ̣ifatani.
data.translation: Das Schlagholz, das in der Hand des Schleuderers ist, der gerade am Spiel ist, dient also zu drei zwecken: Er schleudert damit das Flugholz, er pariert es in der Luft, und man mißt damit den Abstand zwischen Flugholz und Freistau ab.

rationale: Sense 3 with an inanimate implement performing tasks; instrument-as-actor extension, not a new sense.

summary: example for sense 1b in ko-Preterit (97/57)

data.turoyo: Ya, Sətti Bədur, ono ste kəḥzelax abre d malko no w meni w ze l babi latle
data.translation: Sitti Bidur, du siehst, ich bin auch ein Königssohn, und außer mir hat mein Vater niemanden

rationale: First ko-Preterit example for construction 1b, preserving kə- and feminine second-person ending.

summary: example for sense 2 in Infectum-wa (112/13)

data.turoyo: Kul yawmo ḥozewayni ṣaydo, rowaḥwa lebi, adyawma qṭəʕlux u naṣib diḏi, ḥatta disa d ak kulayḏi daʕiri, xəd meqəm.
data.translation: Jeden Tag habe ich Wildpret gefunden, und es wurde mir wohl ums Herz; heute aber hast du mir meinen Anteil vorenthalten, so daß mein Kummer wiedergekommen ist, wie zuvor.

rationale: Sparse Infectum-wa finding cell; habitual reading and distinctive -wayni form.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit-wa (112/49)

data.turoyo: Komər qrele l Kalaš ʕAli, lu abro, d kətwe mi barriye, d ḥzewayle. Məlle: “Ya abri, halux, ʕbar li odaṯe, d siməlli adyawma, laḥ ḥadode d babux, mə ʕaqəl diḏux gqoṭəʕ mena?”
data.translation: Dann rief er Kalasch Ali, den Sohn aus der Steppe, den er gefunden hatte, und sprach: Mein Sohn! Komm, geh in dieses Zimmer hinein, das ich heute von den Schmieden deines Vaters habe machen lassen. Was hältst du davon? -

rationale: Sparse cumulative Preterit-wa finding cell; relative clause describes the adopted child already found.

summary: example for sense 2 in Infectum-wa (115/249)

data.turoyo: Lo kəmmət, hanək šawʕo əšne, kul šato saymowa u qenayḏa w saymowa af farxayḏa, ktowənwa hawxa, ha! Əšmo d meqəm, me d fayiri b kmo yawme, gdəṯyowa, ḥəzyowa: ga kale u qenayḏa xalyo w l əḏʕowa, mən koṯalle, mən koxalle, aydarbo kəzzehən, l əḏʕowa.
data.translation: Seit sieben Jahren nämlich baute sie sich ihr Nest und brütete ihre Jungen aus, und dann plötzlich, wenige Tage bevor sie flügge werden, fand sie immer, wenn sie kam, ihr Nest leer und wußte nie, was da kam und sie fraß, und wie sie verschwanden.

rationale: Sparse Infectum-wa finding cell: habitual discovery of nest empty, contrasting with object-only finding.

summary: example for sense 2 in Infectum-wa (116/42)

data.turoyo: Omər: "Lebux yo, abri. Ono? Hano u medano latyo naṣib diḏi. Gud owewa ṇaṣib diḏi, ono gḥozewayno mede hawxa."
data.translation: Wie du willst, mein Sohn. Ich? Nein! Dies ist nicht für mich bestimmt; wenn es für mich bestimmt wäre, so hätte ich so etwas gefunden.

rationale: Fifth cumulative Infectum-wa sense-2 context, including the moved JL example; clear counterfactual finding.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit (Talay 1/305)

data.turoyo: U qašo ḥazi!
data.translation: Der Pfarrer wurde gefunden

rationale: Sparse Detransitive Preterit finding cell: an independent direct announcement with third-person patient in both source and edition.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit (Talay 1/307)

data.turoyo: I bəšrayḏi aʕlux, qašo Malke ḥazi!
data.translation: Ich gebe euch eine gute Nachricht, der Pfarrer Malke ist gefunden worden.

rationale: Sparse Detransitive Preterit finding cell; complete independent news announcement.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit-wa (Talay 2/21)

data.turoyo: i warqo, d ḥəzyowayle
data.translation: Das Blatt, das er gefunden hatte

rationale: Sparse cumulative Preterit-wa sense 2; feminine patient vocalism retained against masculine variant in interviewer wording.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit-wa (Jan 1.37/1544)

data.turoyo: Ǧan: ʕAmmo Išoʕ mərloxli ʕal i ʕito dak kaldoye d ḥəzyolox, mən šəkəl ḥəzyowalox?
data.translation: Jan: Uncle Isho, you told me about that church of the Chaldeans which you have seen; in what condition had you seen it?

rationale: Thin Preterit-wa sense-1 cell; adjacent active Preterit and Preterit-wa with feminine object; preserve source -wa-lox.

summary: example for sense 1b in Preterit (Jan 1.36/1506)

data.turoyo: Hawxa mədone hawi, ḥzelox?
data.translation: Such things happened, you see?

rationale: Thin round-1 Preterit attention cell 1b; short closing appeal, masculine -ox beside earlier -ux.

summary: example for sense 1b in Preterit (Jan 2.15/3516)

data.turoyo: Ḥzelox, šəmaliye yo, bi diwanxana.
data.translation: Look, it is on the north, in the reception room.

rationale: Thin Preterit 1b cell: spatial explanation rather than an event of having seen.

summary: example for sense 1b in Imperativ (Jan 2.4/1005)

data.turoyo: Darbo d Ḥalab, ḥzay, tamo we i naqqayo.
data.translation: The Aleppo route, you see, it was there at that time.

rationale: Thin Imperativ 1b cell: a parenthetical call inside the clause.

summary: example for sense 2b in Infectum-wa (Jan 2.5/1339)

data.turoyo: Xori Brahim: E, baʕ lə ḥuzanwo ṭaw. (Gaḥxo). Baʕ balki ḥuzanwo ṭaw.
data.translation: Father Brahim: Yes, indeed, they did not see well... perhaps they saw well.

rationale: First Infectum-wa 2b example; retain ambiguous object as a question, with both tokens in one quotation.

summary: example for sense 2b in Preterit (Jan 2.21/3877)

data.turoyo: Yaʕni haṯe ḥəzyoli mede, mqadroli ġalabe.
data.translation: That is, I regarded this as something, I valued it greatly.

rationale: Thin Preterit 2b cell; feminine demonstrative object and valuation context.

summary: example for sense 2b in Preterit (Jan 2.21/3966)

data.turoyo: Ǧan: Yaʕni u medano lə ḥzele manṭəqi?
data.translation: Jan: That is, he did not see this thing as reasonable?

rationale: Thin Preterit 2b cell; explicit object and manṭəqi predicate.

summary: example for sense 2b in Preterit (Jan 3.7/78)

data.turoyo: U šəwolo kule mġamġəmo ḥzeli.
data.translation: I found the whole affair obscure.

rationale: Thin Preterit 2b cell; preverbal object and predicate in written exposition.

summary: example for sense 2b in Preterit (Jan 4.I/197)

data.turoyo: W u medano ḥzeli ġalabe ġalabe muhim d misəm.
data.translation: And I saw it as very, very important that this be done.

rationale: Completes Preterit 2b to five cumulative examples; adjective plus action-content complement.

summary: example for sense 2b in Infectum (Jan 4.II/666)

data.turoyo: Mawxa adyawma u maṯyo da ʕlaymoṯani gaboruṯo rabṯo kḥuzyalla.
data.translation: So today I see the coming of these young women as great courage.

rationale: Unusual feminine observer form kḥuzyalla with indexed object and nominal predicate; useful beyond the already full Infectum 2b cell.

summary: German accusative ending: jene Mann → jenen Mann
rationale: The object of “gesehen hätten” is masculine accusative singular: “jenen Mann”. The supplied translation at 63/308 has that ending.

summary: German noun typo: Absieht → Absicht
rationale: “Absieht” is a misspelling of the noun “Absicht” in “was seine Absicht ist”. The supplied corpus translation repeats the same typo, so this correction follows the unambiguous German word and the Turoyo maqṣad, not the erroneous corpus spelling.

summary: New idiom: ḥzele/ḥoze xēr (mit m-) ‘Gutes erfahren, Nutzen haben’

data.headword: ḥzele/ḥoze xēr (mit m-) ‘Gutes erfahren, Nutzen haben’
data.turoyo: Faqiro hiye laltaḥ yo hiya lalʕal yo, tə=xēr-ze lə=gḥoze, amma aṯi.
data.translation: Der Ärmste, er war unten und sie war oben, er hatte keinerlei Nutzen davon, doch er kam.

rationale: Searched xēr across glossary: nqy quotes the combination but no existing ḥzy idiom; experience-benefit construction.

summary: New idiom: ḥzele/ḥoze ḥəlmo ‘einen Traum haben’

data.turoyo: Ḥzeli ḥəlmo.
data.translation: Ich habe einen Traum gehabt

rationale: Search and supplied idiom inventory show no duplicate ḥzy headword; two consecutive dream-object attestations.

summary: New idiom: ḥzele/ḥoze ʕuǧbo (mit m-) ‘Wunder sehen, sich wundern über’

data.headword: ḥzele/ḥoze ʕuǧbo (mit m-) ‘Wunder sehen, sich wundern über’
data.turoyo: kḥoze ʕuǧbo mu šuġlaṯṯe.
data.translation: Er sah sein Wunder an ihrem Treiben

rationale: Repeated wonder-object combination in several texts; no existing indexed collocation in glossary search.

summary: New idiom: ḥzele/ḥoze raḥa (mit m-ruḥo) ‘Erleichterung erfahren’

data.turoyo: kit alfo naxwaš w nakar d knuṭri u lalyo d toyəm d owe imomo d ḥozən raḥa mə ruḥayye.
data.translation: Es gibt tausend Kranke und Bedürftige, die darauf warten, dass die Nacht zu Ende geht und es Tag wird, damit sie sich besser fühlen.

rationale: Light verb plus relief noun; lookup has other relief expressions but no ḥzy collocation.

summary: New idiom: ḥzele/ḥoze ruḥe ‘wieder Fuß fassen, sich etablieren’

data.headword: ḥzele/ḥoze ruḥe ‘wieder Fuß fassen, sich etablieren’
data.turoyo: w bi gave ḥzalle ruḥayye.
data.translation: und schon bald es ging ihnen gut.

rationale: One clear contextual attestation of reflexive recovery after displacement; distinct from existing self-importance idiom. Conventionality remains a question.

summary: New idiom: ḥzele/ḥoze pežən (mit m-) ‘ein Zeichen, eine Nachricht von jdm. wahrnehmen’

data.headword: ḥzele/ḥoze pežən (mit m-) ‘ein Zeichen, eine Nachricht von jdm. wahrnehmen’
data.turoyo: Faqaṭ azzeyo yarḥo, yarḥo w fəlge, tre yarḥe, tloṯo yarḥe, l aṯi xabro mu gawro w lo ḥzela pežən mine.
data.translation: so verging doch ein Monat, anderthalb Monate zwei Monate, drei Monate, ohne daß Nachricht von dem Gatten kam, und es war nichts von ihm zu sehen und zu hören.

rationale: Glossary search pežən found phrases under sym/fyš/hwy, but none under ḥzy; active seeing with sign object and source.

summary: New idiom: lo ḥzelilux w lo ḥzeluxli ‘ich habe dich nicht gesehen und du mich nicht’, Formel des gegenseitigen Abbruchs

data.headword: lo ḥzelilux w lo ḥzeluxli ‘ich habe dich nicht gesehen und du mich nicht’, Formel des gegenseitigen Abbruchs
data.turoyo: Lo eli ḥzelilux w lo elux ḥzeluxli.
data.translation: Ich habe dich nicht gesehen, und du hast mich nicht gesehen!

rationale: Exact paired formula absent in search; both tokens are one disavowal formula.

summary: New idiom: ḥzele/ḥoze ḥḏoḏe ‘einander treffen, zusammenkommen’

data.turoyo: Aṭ Ṭaya ḥzalle ḥḏoḏe w zbəṭṭe u waziro gab ruḥayye, haw hšuwwe Hetim Ṭayya mede.
data.translation: Die Taiyiten traten zusammen, behielten den Wesir bei sich und rechneten Hatim Tai überhaupt nicht mehr.

rationale: Repeated assembly contexts 111/8,9,32 justify indexing the reciprocal phrase; the separately coordinated consultation verb prevents equating seeing with consulting.

summary: New idiom: ḥzele/ḥoze b-ray ‘für richtig halten, billigen’

data.turoyo: W l aloho hawxa ḥzele bu ray w hawi ḥalwo b ṣadrona di ḥurma d Usuf Paša.
data.translation: Nach Gottes Ratschluss entstand Milch in den Brüsten der Frau von Jusuf Pascha.

rationale: Recurrent b-ray construction in 111/32 and 112/10,22; lookup finds no duplicate headword.

summary: New idiom: ḥzele/ḥoze qurs ‘einen Kurs besuchen, einen Lehrgang absolvieren’

data.headword: ḥzele/ḥoze qurs ‘einen Kurs besuchen, einen Lehrgang absolvieren’
data.turoyo: Xori Brahim: Lo, lo, qurs lə ḥzelan. Qurs di qaṣṭaxana ḥzelan.
data.translation: Father Brahim: No, no, we did not attend a course. We attended the hospital course.

rationale: One verse, contrasting general qurs and hospital training. Course noun plus light verb is indexed here, under I.1; not a new numbered sense. qurs lookup found no existing entry.

summary: New idiom: ḥzele/ḥoze šuġlo (jds.) ‘sich um jds. Angelegenheit kümmern’

data.headword: ḥzele/ḥoze šuġlo (jds.) ‘sich um jds. Angelegenheit kümmern’
data.turoyo: Gədḥuzena šuġle, bas kobəʕ čike d zabno
data.translation: We shall see to his business, but it needs a little time

rationale: One explicit bilingual Turkish/Turoyo parallel supports handling an affair under I.4. Search for the phrase and the baseline/r1 inventories found no duplicate. Hostile intent is contextual, not part of the lexical gloss.

summary: Routine counts strongly favor ordinary I.1 perception: 1337 Preterit and 766 Infectum; I.2 finding has 434 and 79. Counts are supporting frequency evidence, not additional occurrence decisions, and must not be summed again in batch 2.

Experiencers use Preterit l-agent suffixes; objects may be bare NPs, integrated feminine vowels, another l-suffix, or a content/question clause. L-marked lexical agents occur beside suffixes. Avoid assigning agency and patient solely from the edition translation in dense suffix sequences.

Keep active object-predicate evaluation (2b) distinct from the dative-experiencer seeming construction (5). kḥuzele in JTM 5.5/4 plausibly belongs to 5, but its absent translation prevents quoting it.

Preterit-wa has both pre-agent -wo- and post-agent -wa placements. Infectum-wa can express habitual experience, checking, and an unrealized finding outcome. k-/ko- with a Preterit base is ko-Preterit, not a label inferred from German tense.

Detransitive Infectum supports nonvisibility with a theme subject and no expressed viewer (PrS 16/41). Sight nouns, active cognate Infinitiv and finite Detransitive forms must not be conflated merely because the inherited entry groups them together.
Benefit, dream, relief and wonder objects are indexed as collocations under broad seeing/experiencing. A possible Arabic contact parallel is not proof of borrowing or a new verbal sense.

Reader claims of an empty fifth Preterit sense-2 example are not borne out by the supplied parsed entry, which has four substantive examples. No deletion is proposed. Cross-entry form-search hits in ʔzl are quotation co-occurrences, not duplicate root entries.

Batch 2 retains 1b and 2b and all previous corrections. Objectless attention Imperativ forms provide another manifestation of 1b; active evaluator-plus-predicate examples at 58/182, 77/136, 82/50 and 89/14 reinforce 2b.

Reciprocal ḥzalle ḥḏoḏe recurs in assembly contexts 111/8,9,32. Index meeting as a collocation; the separately stated mšawarre consultation shows that the reciprocal phrase itself need not mean confer.

Sense 3 is now supported by Preterit and Infectum: human service/work, metonymic body-part actors, and an implement serving three functions. Do not create separate numbered senses for each actor type.
Finite Detransitive ḥazi supplies agentless finding announcements (Talay 1/304,305,307), distinct from appearance to an experiencer; it does not resolve whether Detransitive 3 is lexically separate.

The repeated routine_counts are the same aggregate support as in batch 1, not another 2800+ distinct occurrences. This decisions file contains exactly the 137 occurrences in batch 2; earlier 150 decisions remain in the named predecessor directory.

New reconstruction of a first-person suffix, a masculine/feminine agreement alternation, or an invariant complement cannot be established solely from a German person change. Preserve the edition spellings and flag ambiguity instead.
No correction to another root is proposed for nys at 115/301 versus supplied 115/307: it lies outside this entry and source numbering needs concordance.

This Jan material includes oral interviews and written discussion. Its editorial/theological register supplies essence, need, institutional affairs and explicit bilingual Turkish parallels; register alone is not evidence for a new verbal meaning.

Preterit observer -li/-lox and feminine patient -yo occur together. ḥəzyolox at Jan 1.38/1608 is active Preterit, not a participle or Detransitive. Contrast with prefixed məḥzəyowa and məḥze, which have theme subjects and no expressed observer.

The omitted source tokens inside long supplied verses are contextual evidence, not extra decision items. Every input occurrence, including repetitions of the same source/form, has its own line in input order.

Round-1 move of the beauty example to Detransitive Infectum is retained without repeating its correction. Detransitive Infectum-wa is newly exemplified at Jan 1.12/450; Jan 2.4/878 is only supporting, uncertain evidence.

ḥzoyo at Jan 2.21/3900 and 2.23/4036 belongs with active Infinitiv, following round 1. A possessive suffix whose referent is seen does not alone establish a Detransitive form. ḥzayto at Jan 4.II/768 is an attitude/viewpoint noun with aʕla, not decisive finite Detransitive evidence.

The course and handling-an-affair expressions are proposed as collocations, each with one source. Turkish contact is suggested by explicit parallel wording in the latter; no claim of historical borrowing is made.
JTM 3.2/36: is ʕƏǧbo kḥuzyono an evaluator construction as provisionally filed in 2b, or another idiomatic expression?
JTM 5.5/4 has no verse_translation. Supply the matching edition translation before adding kḥuzele; do not reuse a line from a different verse without checking alignment.
24/147: the second object is u šayro, but German reads Vogel. Check the source edition and the dʕr/hwy quotations before any text or translation correction.
Does reciprocal ḥzy ḥḏoḏe in Bilgic Die Rolle /42 conventionally mean confer, or simply meet? German berieten sich alone cannot establish consultation.
Is ḥzy ruḥo in JTM 3.2/27 a conventional recovery expression, and how broadly can it mean regaining economic stability?
Clarify the boundary of I.1 encountering and I.2 finding, particularly 54/49 versus 54/7 and JTM 1.5/57; no mass reassignment is justified here.
Check ḥzelax addressed to a boy (Hors 2/19); ḥzallux (Hors 2/79); ḥəzyowaynole (Hors 2/136); and the distribution of ḥəzy- versus ḥoz-.
Check the actor/patient order in PrS 27/36 ḥzelelox, PrS 78/77 Ḥəzyola, and PrS 16/35 /37/84 /37/88 ḥzalle with singular agent and plural patient. Preserve all source spellings.
Check ḥəzyulle/ḥzəyulle feminine-object shapes, Ḥzanxu, ḥzilanne, and contracted ḥozena; their written shapes alone do not settle segmentation.
PrS 14/8: what does feminine -o resume in ḥəzyoli, and is ayko wa a content question or location? PrS 15/91: confirm the Preterit-looking ḥzele in a prospective negative purpose clause.
Confirm agent direction in PrS 72/18 kḥəzele l more dak kallat; and the masculine -le resuming feminine ṣərṭa in MAC NE Habirman Xatun/8.
MM/PrS and Lehrbuch/JL use different reference systems. Existing prs 113/34 and prs 128/37 are not proven citation errors merely because supplied equivalents are PrS 41/35 and 45/9.
The inherited question distinguishing Detransitive 3 appearing from being seen remains open; this batch supplies no decisive new appearing event.
69/176 explicitly lacks a Ritter translation; the supplementary English must not be used as an edition quotation.
35/23 and 78/142 support propositional judgment under broad 1; do editors want a separate construction label only after comparing a wider set of seeing/knowing frames?
Does the paired negative formula at 69/559 cancel dealings, claims, obligations, or only acknowledge a parting? Do not infer a narrower legal meaning.
Check b-ray composition and force, including divine consent in 112/10,22 versus human evaluation in 111/32.
Check the person variation in ḥozino (52/95), ono ḥozena (66/287), ḥozina (113/102), and first-person mə ḥozeno in a third-person narration (78/28). No silent emendation is made.
Confirm b- stimulus versus circumstantial domain at 40/17 bi xədmayḏe and 115/189 bi ṣpahitiyaṯe.
Talay 1/35 lo ḥzeli ruḥi remains unresolved. Likewise 1/164-165 does not by itself prove a lexical come-to-consciousness sense.
The person/gender mismatch in 78/190 ḥzele and missing expected -t in 84/30 ḥoze need edition/native review; compare later feminine forms and the second-person control context.

All Jan English is project machine translation. Obtain an editorial/native translation before treating these quotations as edition evidence, especially Jan 2.5/1339, whose English see well does not resolve the evaluative object.
Jan 2.4/878: is Məḥzenawo we were visible or a local active we used to see? The supplied English chooses active, but the m-prefix and scene do not settle it. No quotation is added from this token.
Jan 2.35/5614: confirm Detransitive Infectum məḥzət amin as be found trustworthy (2), versus show oneself/appear (3); neither the machine rendering nor its tense settles the distinction.
Jan 2.3/441 and 2.17/3614: distinguish finding oneself grown, coming to awareness, recovering ones position and having time/opportunity. Round-1 recovery idiom does not resolve these local readings.
Jan 2.2/203 me ruḥe and 2.17/3644 ʕam ruḥi: confirm self-provision versus self-assessment, and whether private deliberation is conventional. No new numbered senses are proposed.
Jan 2.8/2029 and 2.19/3761: distinguish Preterit ḥzeli from an attention or recall expression, including possible false starts. No productive Imperativ -li paradigm is inferred.

Check segmentation/person of kḥuzewolən (Jan 1.6/93), ḥzallox (Jan 2.20/3847), ḥuzene (Jan 2.34/5506), ḥozenanne (Jan 3.41/1190), and feminine kḥuzyalla/kḥuzyalle. Retain spelling, and do not infer participial status from English perfect wording.
At Jan 2.4/913, who or what does -le in ḥuzewole resume? The truncated xəd... is insufficient for a new Infectum-wa sense-4 quotation.
Does qurs ḥzy conventionally mean attending training, and does šuġlo ḥzy carry any hostile force outside the quoted dispute? The proposed collocation glosses deliberately make no punishment claim.
Collective or metonymic experiencers: districts stand for inhabitants; Midyat encounters a recorder. This changes the participant, not the meaning.

evidence.cite: Bilgic Die Rolle Məḏyaḏs im Tur Abdin/42

summary: Interrogative, reported, auditory and tactile contents extend ordinary perception/ascertainment without requiring a separate epistemic or hearing sense.

evidence.cite: Bilgic Lieber einen Gesellen als einen Prinzen/22
MAC NI Aḥmad Aġa Oṣman Aġa/68

summary: Abstract fərṣa is an opportunity perceived; no distinct seize-an-opportunity meaning is demonstrated by the verb alone.
Fingers can be actors of performing tasks by a body-part metonymy; hands occur as instruments with b-.
Service xadame and the implement carrying out three tasks extend the established work-doing construction; instrument as subject does not create another sense.
Truth can be personified as finding its place; trouble can name a person found. These vary the participants of finding.
Animals perceive humans and a mare detects added weight. Auditory or bodily information may be introduced with ḥzy plus a content clause.
Jan repeatedly supports round-1 object-plus-predicate evaluation, including reflexive ruḥe with identity predicates. Do not propose it again or equate every reflexive use with conceit.
Masculine Preterit ḥzelox, parenthetical Imperativ ḥzay and plural Infectum Koḥozutu extend round-1 attention construction across forms.
xer/xerat with a possessor or m-source supports round-1 benefit collocation; dreaming and reciprocal meeting also recur, without new idiom proposals.
Hunger, fear, hardship, institutional harm and difficulty are experiences already covered by erleben. Sound, singing, reading-mediated worlds and abstract needs extend the contents of perception.
Opportunity, a way and a solution are abstract found objects. Do not multiply senses for these participants or repeat round-1 opportunity notes as a new sense.
